actions.name: Measure home vital signs (temp, HR, BP, RR, SpO2)
actions.result: Temp 98.4°F (36.9°C), HR 78 bpm, BP 112/70 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 99% on room air

actions.name: Camera inspection of surgical incisions (4 laparoscopic port sites)
actions.result: Four port-site incisions on abdomen, each covered with clean dry dressings/steri-strips; edges well-approximated, no redness, swelling, drainage, or gaping seen on camera

actions.name: Pain assessment (0-10 scale, location, triggers)
actions.result: Pain 3/10 at incision sites, described as sore/pulling; occasional sharp pain at right shoulder tip; pain improves with position change and lying down

actions.result: Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN, Oxycodone 5 mg PO q4-6h PRN breakthrough pain, Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q8h PRN, Docusate 100 mg PO BID (stool softener), no other scheduled meds

actions.name: Review operative/discharge note
actions.result: Uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy performed yesterday for acute non-perforated appendicitis; EBL minimal; patient discharged same evening tolerating clears; follow-up with surgeon in 2 weeks

actions.name: Bowel function, GI symptom, and medication adherence screen
actions.result: No bowel movement in 3 days (since before surgery); reports bloating and feeling 'full'; passing flatus intermittently; no nausea or vomiting; no blood in stool reported. When asked generally about taking her medications as prescribed, patient is initially vague about the stool softener and says she has 'mostly' kept up with her meds; a more direct, rapport-based follow-up question may be needed to clarify actual docusate adherence.

actions.name: Camera inspection of lower extremities for swelling/redness (DVT screen)
actions.result: No calf swelling, redness, or warmth seen bilaterally; patient denies calf pain on self-palpation

actions.name: Respiratory and cardiac symptom screen
actions.result: No shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, or cough; shoulder-tip pain is positional and musculoskeletal in character, not exertional

actions.name: Mobility and activity level check
actions.result: Ambulating independently around apartment several times a day; no dizziness or falls; climbing stairs once daily without difficulty

actions.name: Home safety and support screen
actions.result: Lives alone; partner visits evenings and can assist as needed; has phone/emergency contacts accessible; no immediate safety concerns identified

actions.name: Review most recent inpatient vital signs flowsheet
actions.result: Last recorded vitals prior to discharge: Temp 98.2°F, HR 74 bpm, BP 118/72 mmHg, RR 14/min, SpO2 100% - all within normal limits

actions.name: Medication reconciliation and OTC product screen
actions.result: Patient reports taking a daytime cold/flu combination product for a scratchy throat, two doses so far today, in addition to her two scheduled 650 mg acetaminophen doses for incision pain. She does not think the cold product 'counts' as real medicine. Based on her report, today's acetaminophen intake so far is approximately 1950 mg (1300 mg scheduled + ~650 mg from the cold product, pending confirmation of its acetaminophen content). If she continues this same pattern for the rest of the day (2 more scheduled 650 mg doses = 1300 mg more, plus 2 more cold-product tablets = 650 mg more), her projected 24-hour acetaminophen total could reach approximately 3900 mg - well above the 3000-3250 mg/24h safe maximum, creating a hepatotoxicity risk that needs same-day correction.

actions.name: Skin and surgical site temperature check via patient palpation
actions.result: Patient reports skin around incisions feels normal temperature, not hot to touch; no increased warmth noted

artifacts.title: Operative & Discharge Summary
artifacts.author: Dr. L. Chen, General Surgery
artifacts.body: 28-year-old female s/p uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy for acute non-perforated appendicitis. Procedure performed without complication, estimated blood loss minimal. Four 5-12mm port incisions closed with absorbable sutures/steri-strips. Tolerated clear liquids post-op, ambulated same day, voided without difficulty. Discharged home post-op day 0 in stable condition. Instructed on incision care, activity restrictions (no heavy lifting >10 lbs x2 weeks, may shower after 24 hours, no driving while taking opioids), and return precautions. Follow-up with surgery clinic in 2 weeks for wound check.

artifacts.title: Over-the-counter and combination product the patient is taking
artifacts.body: Patient-reported product: 'DayQuil-type' daytime cold and flu combination tablet. Label lists: Acetaminophen 325 mg, Dextromethorphan HBr 10 mg, Phenylephrine HCl 5 mg per tablet. Patient has taken 2 tablets so far today (first dose this morning, second dose at lunchtime) in addition to two scheduled 650 mg acetaminophen doses for incision pain. Measured intake so far today: approximately 1950 mg acetaminophen (1300 mg scheduled + 650 mg from cold product). Projected 24-hour total if she continues this same pattern (2 more scheduled 650 mg doses = 1300 mg, plus 2 more cold-product tablets = 650 mg) is approximately 3900 mg - well above the safe maximum of 3000-3250 mg/24h, representing a significant overdose risk that requires same-day correction.

artifacts.title: Prior Nursing Discharge Teaching Note
artifacts.author: RN, inpatient surgical unit
artifacts.body: Patient and partner present for discharge teaching. Verbalized understanding of incision care (keep dry 24h, then may shower, pat dry, no soaking/baths or swimming until cleared by surgeon), activity restrictions (no lifting >10 lbs, no driving for 24-48h or while on opioids, gradual return to normal activity over 1-2 weeks), and return precautions (fever >101°F, increasing redness/drainage/odor from incision, severe or worsening abdominal pain, no bowel movement by day 3-4 with worsening distension, chest pain or shortness of breath, calf swelling/pain). Written instructions provided. Follow-up appointment scheduled.

objectives.text: Perform a focused post-operative assessment via telehealth including vital signs review, pain assessment, and camera-based wound inspection appropriate for a remote visit.

Identify and educate the patient about safe combined analgesic use, recognizing the risk of unintentional acetaminophen overdose from combining scheduled acetaminophen with an OTC combination product.
Differentiate benign expected post-laparoscopic symptoms (shoulder-tip gas pain, mild constipation) from concerning findings requiring escalation, and know when to involve the surgical team.
Provide clear patient education on constipation management, activity restrictions (showering, driving, lifting), and incision care appropriate to post-op day 1.

Recognize red-flag/return precaution symptoms for post-appendectomy patients and demonstrate appropriate SBAR escalation to the provider when a safety concern (e.g., analgesic overdose risk) is identified.

mismatches.patientClaim: Priya says she's 'just taking the cold medicine and my regular pain pills like they told me, nothing extra' and doesn't think the cold tablets count as a real medication.
mismatches.recordEvidence: The cold/flu combination product label (artifact d5) shows it contains 325 mg acetaminophen per tablet. Her measured intake today so far (two scheduled 650 mg doses plus two cold-product tablets) is already about 1950 mg, and if she continues this same dosing pattern for the rest of the day, her projected 24-hour acetaminophen total would reach approximately 3900 mg - well above the 3000-3250 mg/24h safe maximum, risking hepatotoxicity if not corrected now.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients often do not recognize that OTC cold/flu combination products contain acetaminophen, leading to unintentional overdose when combined with prescribed scheduled acetaminophen. Nurses must specifically ask about all OTC products, calculate both the current measured intake and the projected 24-hour total based on the patient's dosing pattern, and intervene before the safe maximum is reached.

patient.name: Priya Nair
patient.appearance: A young woman with shoulder-length dark hair pulled into a loose bun, sitting propped up on pillows on her couch wearing a loose grey t-shirt. The room is softly lit with daylight through a window; she shifts position a few times during the call and holds a hand loosely over her lower abdomen when she laughs or moves.

persona.personality: Pleasant, cooperative, and a little anxious about doing things 'right' during recovery; appreciates clear, simple explanations.
persona.communicationStyle: Talks in full sentences, asks follow-up questions, sometimes downplays discomfort to seem like a 'good patient' but will answer honestly when asked directly.
persona.emotionalState: Mildly anxious about the shoulder pain and unsure if she is recovering normally; otherwise in good spirits.
persona.background: Priya works remotely as a graphic designer for a tech startup in Austin. She moved from Chicago two years ago, lives alone in a one-bedroom apartment, and has a partner who stops by most evenings after work. She enjoys yoga and cooking but has had to pause both since surgery. Her parents live out of state and she has been keeping them updated by phone.
speechExamples: I feel okay, just kind of sore and bloated, like I ate too much even though I haven't eaten much at all.
This weird pain in my shoulder is kind of freaking me out, is that normal?
I didn't think the cold medicine counted as 'real' medicine since you can just buy it at the store.
Can I shower today? I feel kind of gross.
I don't want to take too many pain pills, so I've just been pushing through it mostly.
concerns: I'm worried this shoulder pain might be my heart—is that normal?
I haven't had a bowel movement in three days and I feel really bloated. Is that okay?
When am I allowed to shower and get the dressings wet?
When can I drive again and go back to lifting things at work?

scenario.studentBrief: You are the RN conducting a telehealth discharge follow-up call with Priya Nair, 28, who had an uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy yesterday. She was discharged the same day. Your goals are to perform a focused post-operative assessment, screen for complications, and provide discharge teaching.

Determine whether any findings require SBAR escalation to the surgical provider.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Expected post-operative day 1 recovery after uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy, with two actionable nursing concerns: (1) risk of unintentional acetaminophen overdose from combining scheduled acetaminophen with an OTC combination cold product if the current dosing pattern continues through the day, and (2) early post-operative constipation with inconsistent stool softener use requiring teaching and monitoring.
differential: Normal expected recovery with benign referred shoulder-tip pain from laparoscopic CO2 insufflation (most likely explanation for shoulder symptom)
Post-operative ileus/constipation from opioid use and reduced fiber/fluid intake (explains bloating and 3-day stool absence)

Unintentional supratherapeutic acetaminophen dosing projected over 24 hours from combined scheduled and OTC product use (safety concern requiring immediate teaching/escalation before the maximum is reached)
Less likely: cardiac or pulmonary cause of shoulder pain (reassuring given absence of chest pain, dyspnea, exertional pattern, and normal vitals)
Less likely: surgical site infection or intra-abdominal complication (reassuring given clean dry wound on camera, afebrile, soft non-rigid abdomen, improving pain trend)
keyFindings: Incisions clean, dry, well-approximated on camera inspection
Mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without rigidity or guarding
No bowel movement in 3 days with bloating; passing flatus intermittently
Shoulder-tip pain is positional, non-exertional, without chest pain or dyspnea - consistent with referred gas pain
Patient has not been reliably taking prescribed stool softener as directed

Patient's measured acetaminophen intake today (~1950 mg) is combining a scheduled regimen with an OTC cold remedy; if this pattern continues, her projected 24-hour total (~3900 mg) would substantially exceed the safe maximum, requiring same-day correction
No signs of DVT, infection, or cardiopulmonary compromise
plan: Educate patient that shoulder-tip pain is a common, expected effect of residual CO2 gas from laparoscopic surgery irritating the diaphragm, and reassure regarding cardiac concern given reassuring exam/vitals/ROS, while advising her to report any chest pain, shortness of breath, or worsening symptoms immediately

Educate on safe acetaminophen dosing: stop the OTC combination cold product or reduce scheduled acetaminophen so that the projected total daily acetaminophen (prescribed + OTC) does not exceed the safe maximum (generally 3000-3250 mg/24h); advise reading labels of all OTC products for hidden acetaminophen before her current measured intake (~1950 mg) progresses to the projected at-risk total (~3900 mg) later today

Resume and reinforce adherence to prescribed docusate stool softener; encourage increased fluid intake, gentle ambulation, and gradual reintroduction of fiber (fruits, vegetables, whole grains) to address constipation
Advise if no bowel movement within another 24-48 hours despite measures, or if abdominal distension/pain worsens, to contact the surgical provider

Provide activity teaching: may shower now that >24 hours have passed since surgery (per discharge instructions), pat incisions dry, no soaking/baths/swimming until surgeon clears; no driving for 24-48h or while taking oxycodone; no lifting greater than 10 lbs for 2 weeks (clarify with patient regarding lifting her cat)
Reinforce incision care: keep clean and dry, monitor daily for increasing redness, warmth, swelling, drainage, odor, or wound separation

Reinforce red-flag return precautions: fever over 101°F, worsening or severe abdominal pain, inability to pass stool/gas with worsening distension, chest pain or shortness of breath, calf swelling or pain, incision changes - seek care immediately if these occur

Document focused assessment and education using nursing note format; communicate the projected acetaminophen dosing safety concern to the surgical provider via SBAR for awareness and to confirm a safe analgesic plan going forward before the projected maximum is reached
Schedule or confirm follow-up with surgery clinic in 2 weeks per discharge plan; encourage patient to call sooner if any red-flag symptoms develop
redFlags: Increasing abdominal pain, rigidity, or distension
Signs of wound infection: increasing redness, warmth, swelling, purulent or foul-smelling drainage, wound separation
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or exertional symptoms (to distinguish from benign referred gas pain)
Signs of DVT: calf swelling, pain, warmth, redness
No bowel movement or flatus with worsening distension, nausea, or vomiting suggesting ileus/obstruction
Signs/symptoms of acetaminophen toxicity: right upper quadrant pain, nausea, jaundice (relevant given projected combined OTC/prescribed dosing)
educationPoints: OTC combination cold and flu products frequently contain acetaminophen; patients should always check active ingredients to avoid unintentional overdose when also taking scheduled acetaminophen, especially before the day's dosing pattern pushes the projected total well over the safe maximum

Shoulder-tip pain after laparoscopic surgery is a well-recognized, benign, self-limited symptom caused by residual CO2 gas irritating the diaphragm and phrenic nerve, typically resolving within a few days
Opioid analgesics and reduced oral intake commonly contribute to post-operative constipation; stool softeners should be taken as prescribed proactively rather than only once symptoms develop
Clear, specific activity guidance (showering, driving, lifting thresholds) reduces patient anxiety and supports safe recovery adherence

Nursing assessment via telehealth can effectively screen for post-operative complications using camera-based wound inspection, guided self-palpation, and structured symptom review, with escalation to the provider when a projected safety concern is identified before it becomes an actual overdose

profile.title: Post-operative day 1 telehealth follow-up after laparoscopic appendectomy in a 28-year-old with acetaminophen overdose risk
profile.summary: A 28-year-old woman one day after uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy presents for routine discharge follow-up. She is recovering well but has inadvertently combined prescribed paracetamol with an OTC cold remedy also containing paracetamol, creating overdose risk. She also has typical post-operative constipation and referred shoulder-tip gas pain she fears is cardiac. This case teaches safe post-operative assessment via telehealth, medication reconciliation to identify polypharmacy risks, and differentiation of expected recovery findings from complications requiring escalation.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit; patient's apartment in Austin
